findings: 320 physical pixels were displayed in bubbles up to 320 points tall; 3x screens need up to 960 pixels.
Every row reopen resolved a server target before checking local preview bytes.
A seeded row repeated borrowing and decoding after the store had already produced an authorized image.
Local timeline publication followed draft restoration and unrelated history/profile/policy reads.
changes: Use the existing bounded 1280px server rendition for chat display and decode at the same size; original remains a separate on-open request.

Retain at most 64 account-session preview authorization records, keyed by message, media and size. Reuse only before expiry and while access generation and current local message access remain valid; verify published local bytes.
Discard, changed rendition identity, tombstones, access-generation changes and account close prevent stale reuse. No persistent authorization or original fallback added.
Publish local timeline after redaction cleanup and before draft/metadata reads; do not gate initial timeline on image loading.
Avoid duplicate decoding of the current seeded file; bound retained decoded store seeds to 16MiB in addition to the existing 32MiB decode cache.

Before publishing an empty local timeline, probe at most 8 recent image references for valid account-local authorization and already decoded pixels. This path never performs media file I/O, starts/joins decoding, resolves a target or waits for network admission. Cache misses are skipped. Initial snapshot contains seeded pixels on hits; stale refresh generations cannot publish seeds.

coverage: Warm preview reopens offline without a second target request or byte transfer
